fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. The LORD says they “…have eyes but do not see…” and “…have ears but do not hear.” (Jeremiah 5:21). The equipment is all there and they still don't see or hear. It's like a phone buzzing in your jacket all afternoon and you never notice.

Close, friend, but forgetting isn't what the LORD says here. He says they “…have eyes but do not see…” and “…have ears but do not hear.” (Jeremiah 5:21). The problem is that they don't see or hear, not that they forget.

Right on. The LORD says “…these people have stubborn and rebellious hearts.” (Jeremiah 5:23). Right before it, He talks about the sea and the sand boundary He set for it (Jeremiah 5:22). Then He turns to His people's hearts.

That's the one. The LORD “…gives the rains, both autumn and spring, in season…” (Jeremiah 5:24). The same verse says He keeps the appointed weeks of harvest. Rains and harvest weeks, both named in one verse.
Frost won't do it, friend. The verse says the LORD “…gives the rains, both autumn and spring, in season…” (Jeremiah 5:24). Frost isn't in that verse at all. I'd keep the frost out of this batch.

Not foxes, friend. The LORD says these wicked men “…set a trap to catch men.” (Jeremiah 5:26). They watch like fowlers, but the ones they're after are people. That's the part that should make you sit up.

Deceit, that's it. The LORD says “Like cages full of birds, so their houses are full of deceit.” (Jeremiah 5:27). A cage full of birds is hard to miss. These houses are just as packed, only with deceit.

Laughter would be a lovely thing to fill a house with, friend, but that's not the verse. The LORD says their houses are full of deceit (Jeremiah 5:27). The picture is a cage packed with birds, and these houses are just as packed, with deceit.

Soldiers aren't named here, friend. The LORD says these men have “…not taken up the cause of the fatherless…” (Jeremiah 5:28). They also haven't defended the rights of the needy. Those are the two the verse names.
That's right, baker. The passage says “The prophets prophesy falsely…” (Jeremiah 5:31). I think that's a heavy line to read.
Leaving the land isn't in the verse, friend. The passage says “The prophets prophesy falsely…” (Jeremiah 5:31). That's what they're doing. Prophesying falsely is the thing the verse names.
Their own, baker. The passage says “…the priests rule by their own authority.” (Jeremiah 5:31). The LORD's and the king's aren't named there. Their own is the one the verse gives.

True, baker. The passage says “My people love it so…” (Jeremiah 5:31). That comes right after the prophets prophesying falsely and the priests ruling by their own authority. That's what makes the closing question hit so hard.
